probe_meta.label: dense-G (controlled retrieval-mechanism swap of Probe G)

response_text:
1. (Currently amended) A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising:
a hardware entropy source;
a processor; and
memory storing instructions that, when executed by the processor, cause the processor to at least:
receive a plurality of independent first entropy values from the hardware entropy source;
apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value;
seed a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
generate a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

2. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the processor being caused to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes being caused to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

3. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the processor being caused to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes being caused to at least:
implement a key-agreement protocol using the random number and in which a key is produced; and
produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the key.

4. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware entropy source is a ring oscillator, and the processor being caused to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values includes being caused to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator.

5. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware entropy source is a single hardware source, and the processor being caused to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values includes being caused to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware source.

6. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware entropy source comprises a plurality of independent hardware sources, and the processor being caused to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values includes being caused to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent hardware sources.

7. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a permutation function, and the processor being caused to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being caused to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

8. (Currently amended) The system of claim 7, wherein the processor being caused to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being caused to:
divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenate the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a hash function, and the processor being caused to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being caused to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function.

10. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and the processor being caused to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being caused to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

11. (Currently amended) The system of claim 1, wherein the processor being caused to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes being caused to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

12. (Cancelled)

13. (Currently amended) A method of providing security in a computer system, comprising:
receiving a plurality of independent first entropy values from a hardware entropy source;
applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value;
seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value;
generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and
producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

14. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

15. (Original)

16. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware entropy source is a ring oscillator, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator.

17. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware entropy source is a single hardware source, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware source.

18. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the hardware entropy source comprises a plurality of independent hardware sources, and wherein receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values includes receiving the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent hardware sources.

19. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a permutation function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

20. (Currently amended) The method of claim 19, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes:
dividing the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values;
applying the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and
concatenating the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

21. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a hash function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function.

22. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

23. (Currently amended) The method of claim 13, wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes selectively applying multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

24. (Cancelled)
